To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
APP and APPsalpha can protect neurons against acute hypoxia, ischemia and excitotoxicity by modulating NMDA receptors and voltage-gated calcium channel activity and expression.
APP and its soluble extracellular domain, APPsα, are neuroprotective in acute neuronal injuries, including hypoxia-ischaemia and excitotoxicity.
APP and its soluble fragments APPsα can protect neurons from acute insults by regulating calcium homeostasis and by affecting gene expression and neurotrophic factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the role of the amyloid precursor protein in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer’s disease and in the pathophysiology of stroke.
the role of the amyloid precursor protein in acute brain insults.
the role of APP and its soluble fragments in the regulation of neuronal function and survival.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the APP is not only involved in the pathology of neurodegenerative diseases but also in the neuroprotection of the nervous system.
APP has a protective effect in neuronal insults.
APP is a protective factor in acute neuronal insults, but that this protective role of APP may be counteracted by the amyloidogenic processing of APP in the long-term.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
APP is a neuroprotective factor and APPsα is a neuroprotectant.

APP and its proteolytic fragments can be neuroprotective in acute neuronal insults and may therefore be used for the development of new therapeutic strategies for the treatment of TBI or ischemic stroke.

APP may be an important factor in neuroprotection.
